'''Jeremy Keith Burdett''' (July 1, 1947 – June 23, 1997), or '''Jeremy K. Burdett''', was a British-American chemist known for his work on bridging the gap<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Burdett |first=Jeremy K. |date=1979 |title=Application of 'molecular' theories to the structure of the crystalline state |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/279121a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=279 |issue=5709 |pages=121–125 |doi=10.1038/279121a0 |bibcode=1979Natur.279..121B |s2cid=4316999 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> between molecular science and [[Solid-state chemistry|solid state chemistry]] from an [[Molecular orbital|electron orbital]] viewpoint.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1997-09-22 |title=people |journal=Chemical & Engineering News Archive |language=en |volume=75 |issue=38 |pages=83 |doi=10.1021/cen-v075n038.p083 |issn=0009-2347|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Burdett was a native of London, UK. He studied at the [[Magdalene College, Cambridge|Magdalene College]], [[University of Cambridge]], receiving his bachelor's degree in 1968 in natural sciences with a specialization in chemistry. He obtained a master's degree from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1970 and worked as a Power Foundation Fellow with [[Jerry Current]]. He returned to the [[University of Cambridge]] and received a Ph.D. in 1972 under the supervision of Jim J. Turner. Subsequently, Burdett moved to [[Newcastle University]] along with Jim J. Turner's group and was appointed senior research officer. In 1977, Burdett spent a sabbatical at [[Cornell University]] with [[Roald Hoffmann]], who greatly influenced Burdett's research direction. In 1978, Burdett joined the faculty at the [[University of Chicago]], where he spent the rest of his career.<ref name=Polyakoff>{{Cite web |date=1997-07-23 |title=Obituary : Professor Jeremy Burdett |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/obituary-professor-jeremy-burdett-1252237.html |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Burdett received the following accolades during his career,<ref name=Polyakoff /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jeremy K. Burdett: H-index & Awards - Academic Profile |url=https://research.com/u/jeremy-k-burdett |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=Research.com |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Meldola Medal and Prize|Meldola Medals]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (1977) along with [[Martyn Poliakoff]]
* [[Sloan Research Fellow|Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Fellow]] (1979)
* [[Camille and Henry Dreyfus Foundation]] Teacher Scholar
* Fellow of the [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]] (1990)
* Wilsmore Fellow of the [[University of Melbourne]] (1985)
* CNRS Visiting professor at the [[Universite de Paris-Sud]], [[Orsay]] (1987) and at [[University of Rennes 1]] (1994)
* Tilden Medal and Prize of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (1995).

== Personal life ==
Burdett's first wife was Wendy Greenwood, with whom he had two sons, Rufus and Harry.   Burdett died at his summer home in [[Kalamazoo, Michigan]], after attending a conference in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=JEREMY BURDETT, 49, U. OF C. CHEMIST |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1997-06-27-9706270318-story.html |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=Chicago Tribune|date=27 June 1997 }}</ref>
